summary: A low-caffeine pre-workout drink powder from Performance Lab. whatItIs: Pre Lab Pro is a natural-berry-flavoured pre-workout powder sold through performancelab.com; the buy buttons on its own site, prelabpro.com, link to that product page. A tub holds 20 servings of one 13g scoop, mixed into 300ml of water and taken 15-30 minutes before training, with no more than 2 scoops in 24 hours. Each scoop also supplies 500mg Himalayan pink salt, vitamin D3 from algae, B2, B6, folate, B12, potassium and iron. It is vegan, and the vendor states it is 'third-party tested and validated by Informed Sport'; the product page shows no certificate or batch number. EU orders are shipped from the brand's depot in Europe; the shipping page does not list individual EU countries, so confirm delivery to your country at checkout.
howItWorks: Caffeine (80mg) blocks adenosine receptors to dull fatigue signals, and L-theanine (160mg, a 2:1 ratio) plus L-tyrosine (400mg) are the nootropic trio from Performance Lab's Caffeine 2 capsule at higher amounts. L-citrulline is converted to arginine and then nitric oxide, and beetroot supplies dietary nitrate, a second nitric-oxide source; the vendor includes both for blood flow, strength and endurance. Glutathione, an antioxidant, makes up the rest of the Setria for Sport blend. Himalayan pink salt (200mg sodium) and potassium act as electrolytes. Pre Lab Pro itself has not been tested in a published trial; the vendor's claims rest on ingredient-level research. Supplements sold in the EU fall under Directive 2002/46/EC, so the label may carry only EU-authorised health claims, and the EU register holds no authorised caffeine claim for alertness or concentration (a caffeine alertness claim was refused under Regulation (EU) 2016/1411).
whatToExpect: Performance Lab says Pre Lab Pro starts working in around 15-30 minutes. The vendor calls the 80mg caffeine dose moderate, and two scoops (its 24-hour limit) give 160mg; count it toward your daily caffeine total. The citrulline and beet amounts are below the doses used in performance trials, so any blood-flow or endurance benefit from them is uncertain. EU delivery is expected in 4-12 working days depending on destination (per performancelab.com's shipping page, checked 2026-10-05). It is €45 one-time on eu.performancelab.com (20 servings; subscription priced separately; checked 2026-10-08), so confirm the total at checkout.

summary: A caffeine-free 'cellular energy' capsule from Performance Lab: one 2-capsule serving gives 500mg acetyl-L-carnitine, 100mg R-lipoic acid, 100mg CoQ10, 10mg PQQ and 60mg magnesium, with every dose on the label. It is an energy supplement with a modest cognitive angle, not a nootropic stack, and none of its five actives reaches the reference dose in our dosing audit. EU orders ship from the brand's European depot in 4-12 working days (per performancelab.com's shipping page, checked 2026-10-05); it is €59 one-time on eu.performancelab.com (30 servings; subscription priced separately; checked 2026-10-08).
whatItIs: Performance Lab Energy is a caffeine-free capsule sold through performancelab.com. The vendor calls it a 'caffeine-free workout and daily energy supplement' for 'cellular energy, cardio performance, muscle strength, and clean focus'. One serving is 2 vegan pullulan capsules holding 500mg acetyl-L-carnitine (from acetyl-L-carnitine HCl), 100mg microencapsulated BioEnhanced R-lipoic acid, 100mg MicroActive Q10 (coenzyme Q10), 10mg BioPQQ (pyrroloquinoline quinone), 60mg magnesium as magnesium malate (14% of the US Daily Value) and 2.5mg BioPerine black pepper extract (95% piperine), which the vendor adds 'for enhanced absorption'; a bottle holds 30 servings. The label suggests 2 capsules in the morning or early afternoon on an empty stomach. The vendor states it is 'third-party tested for purity and potency' but names no lab. Per performancelab.com's shipping page (checked 2026-10-05), EU orders are shipped from the brand's depot in Europe; the page does not list individual EU countries, so confirm delivery to your country at checkout.
howItWorks: Energy is built around mitochondria, the parts of cells that turn food into usable energy. Acetyl-L-carnitine carries fatty acids into mitochondria and donates acetyl groups for making acetylcholine; its positive cognitive trials used 1.5-3g a day in older adults with mild cognitive impairment, mild dementia or pre-frailty (Montgomery 2003 meta-analysis; Passeri 1990; Malaguarnera 2022), at least three times the 500mg here, and we found no trial in healthy young adults. PQQ improved some memory and attention scores in three small 12-week trials at about 20mg a day (Itoh 2016, Shiojima 2021, Tamakoshi 2023), two of them with authors affiliated with the PQQ manufacturer; Energy has 10mg. The vendor describes CoQ10 and R-lipoic acid as mitochondrial cofactors and antioxidants, but we found no positive cognitive trial of either: 300mg CoQ10 a day did not improve attention or working memory over 6 months in a trial in schizophrenia (Maguire 2021), and 100mg alpha-lipoic acid a day did not improve cognition in the only dose-matched trial we found, also in schizophrenia (De Lima 2023). BioPerine is there to aid absorption; we have not verified whether 2.5mg of piperine changes how well these ingredients are absorbed. Energy itself has not been tested in a published trial. Supplements sold in the EU fall under Directive 2002/46/EC, and the label may carry only health claims authorised under Regulation (EC) No 1924/2006.
whatToExpect: Performance Lab says Energy starts working in around 30 minutes and that you may notice 'increased vitality', more motivation, a brighter mood and better muscle strength and cardio performance during exercise. It contains no caffeine or other stimulant. The positive cognitive trials of acetyl-L-carnitine and PQQ ran for 12 weeks or longer at 2 to 6 times these doses, so any cognitive effect at Energy's doses is uncertain. The label suggests 2 capsules in the morning or early afternoon on an empty stomach; the product page also suggests 2 capsules 30-45 minutes before a workout. EU delivery is expected in 4-12 working days depending on destination (per performancelab.com's shipping page, checked 2026-10-05). It is €59 one-time on eu.performancelab.com (30 servings; subscription priced separately; checked 2026-10-08), so confirm the total at checkout.

whatItIs: Performance Lab Omega-3 is an algae-based omega-3 supplement sold through performancelab.com. The vendor positions it 'to support optimal health and performance of the brain, eyes, heart and (much) more'. One serving is 3 NutriGels, softgels the vendor describes as vegan and free of gelatin and carrageenan (other ingredients listed: gellan gum, pectin, starch and glycerin), holding 1,800mg algal oil from life's OMEGA 60 with 990mg total omega-3 fatty acids, of which 540mg is DHA and 270mg is EPA; a bottle holds 30 servings. The label suggests 3 softgels with your first meal of the day. The vendor states it is 'third-party tested for purity and potency' and Clean Label Project certified; the product page shows the certification logo but no certificate or batch number. Per performancelab.com's shipping page (checked 2026-10-05), EU orders are shipped from the brand's depot in Europe; the page does not list individual EU countries, so confirm delivery to your country at checkout.
howItWorks: DHA is the main structural omega-3 in brain cell membranes. In two 6-month trials it improved memory measures at 900mg a day in adults aged 55 and over with age-related cognitive decline (Yurko-Mauro 2010, sponsored by the algal-DHA maker Martek) and at 1.16g a day in healthy 18-45-year-olds with low DHA intake (Stonehouse 2013); this product supplies 540mg, below both. The wider evidence is mixed: a 2012 Cochrane review found no cognitive benefit from omega-3 supplements in cognitively healthy older adults. We found no trial of EPA alone for cognition; a 2024 dose-response meta-analysis of 24 trials of mixed EPA and DHA in adults aged 40 and over found an executive-function benefit trend above 500mg a day of total omega-3 (Suh 2024), which the 990mg here exceeds. The oil comes from algae rather than fish, so it suits vegans. Performance Lab Omega-3 itself has not been tested in a published trial. Supplements sold in the EU fall under Directive 2002/46/EC, and the label may carry only health claims authorised under Regulation (EC) No 1924/2006.
whatToExpect: Performance Lab says Omega-3 starts working in around 30 minutes, that you may first notice improvements to hair, nails and skin, and that other benefits build over time; both positive DHA memory trials ran for 6 months, so do not expect a quick cognitive effect. Take 3 softgels with your first meal of the day. Our DHA ingredient page notes that in a 2021 meta-analysis of cardiovascular trials, omega-3 supplements were linked to a higher risk of atrial fibrillation, more so above 1g a day; one serving here gives 990mg of total omega-3, so ask your doctor first if you have a heart-rhythm condition or already take another omega-3. EU delivery is expected in 4-12 working days depending on destination (per performancelab.com's shipping page, checked 2026-10-05). It is €45 one-time on eu.performancelab.com (30 servings; subscription priced separately; checked 2026-10-08), so confirm the total at checkout.
pros: Vegan omega-3 from algal oil (life's OMEGA 60) rather than fish
990mg total omega-3 per serving, every amount on the label
Softgels the vendor says are free of gelatin and carrageenan
Ships to EU buyers from a European depot (4-12 working days)
cons: 540mg DHA is below the 900mg-1.2g a day used in the positive DHA memory trials

Ratio wording is inconsistent: the product page mostly describes an 'optimal 2:1 EPA:DHA' ratio, but the label's 540mg DHA and 270mg EPA make it 2:1 DHA to EPA; the page also says one serving provides 900mg of EPA and DHA, while those two label rows add up to 810mg
A general-health omega-3 rather than a nootropic; evidence for omega-3 and cognition in healthy adults is mixed
No published trial of Performance Lab Omega-3 itself; the evidence is for DHA and EPA
Small Trustpilot sample: 14 reviews for performancelab.com (3.8/5, checked 2026-10-05)
30-day money-back guarantee covers the first order only: one container, used up, with the claim filed within 60 days of delivery, refund minus shipping
